question: Which historic international conference officially launched the modern concept of Primary Health Care (PHC) back in 1978?
explanation: Spot on! The 1978 conference in Alma-Ata set the global standard for making basic health services accessible to everyone right in their communities. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T3#GNS124_U1_T3_h1)

question: How did healthcare delivery change globally after Primary Health Care was introduced?

options.A: It focused exclusively on building high-tech specialist hospitals in rural areas
options.B: It transferred all health responsibilities away from governments to private individuals
options.C: It eliminated traditional medicine entirely in favor of imported pharmaceuticals
options.D: It shifted from expensive hospital-centric curative care to community-based preventive care

explanation: You got it! Before PHC, the system waited for people to fall sick and travel far to hospitals. PHC changed this by bringing prevention and basic care directly to the people. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T3#GNS124_U1_T3_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT one of the core principles of Primary Health Care?

options.B: Active community participation in health planning
options.C: Exclusive reliance on advanced foreign technology
options.D: Equitable distribution of essential health services

explanation: Correct! PHC focuses on affordable, appropriate local solutions, not expensive or dependent foreign technology. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T3#GNS124_U1_T3_h2)

question: Why does Primary Health Care require different sectors to work together (intersectoral collaboration)?

options.A: Because the Ministry of Health cannot legally purchase medications without other ministries
options.B: Because doctors need assistance from foreign engineers to run rural clinics
options.C: Because health is influenced by non-medical factors like education, agriculture, and clean water
options.D: Because nurses are required to work in agricultural fields during planting seasons

explanation: Well done! Good health goes beyond medicine. It relies heavily on food security, safe water, and education—which means different government sectors must team up. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T3#GNS124_U1_T3_h2)

question: What is the main difference between equality and equity in healthcare?

options.A: Equity applies only to urban hospitals, while equality applies strictly to rural health posts
options.B: Equality gives everyone the same resources, while equity gives extra support to those with greater needs
options.C: Equity is decided by federal policies, while equality is managed by local community leaders
options.D: Equality focuses on curing diseases, whereas equity focuses entirely on disease prevention

explanation: Exactly! Equity recognizes that people start from different places, so we must distribute resources fairly based on actual needs to achieve true health for all. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T3#GNS124_U1_T3_h3)

question: A local health clinic places its mobile immunization teams in hard-to-reach nomadic settlements instead of the well-served town center. Which PHC principle is this?
explanation: Spot on! Taking services directly to vulnerable, hard-to-reach groups is the true definition of equity in action. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T3#GNS124_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is the main benefit of involving local community members when planning health programs?

options.A: It guarantees that patients will pay high fees for services
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for professional nurses
options.C: It ensures the programs are culturally acceptable and sustainable
options.D: It allows the federal government to stop funding local health centers

explanation: Correct! When communities help design their own health programs, they take ownership and keep them running successfully for the long haul. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T3#GNS124_U1_T3_h4)

question: A community health nurse wants to start a nutrition program in a rural village. What is the best first step following PHC philosophy?

options.A: Build a modern multi-story hospital in the center of the village
options.B: Consult with local community leaders and residents to identify their actual nutritional priorities
options.C: Import expensive foreign dietary supplements and distribute them immediately
options.D: Report the villagers to local authorities for poor feeding habits

explanation: You got it! Community participation always starts by listening to the people first and letting them help identify their own needs and solutions. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T3#GNS124_U1_T3_h4)

question: How is 'appropriate technology' defined in Primary Health Care?

options.A: Traditional herbal remedies that have never been scientifically tested
options.B: The most expensive and advanced medical machinery available on the global market
options.C: Digital computer systems used exclusively in large urban teaching hospitals
options.D: Equipment and methods that are scientifically valid, affordable, and locally maintainable

explanation: Spot on! Appropriate technology hits the sweet spot: it actually works scientifically, but it is also cheap and easy for the local community to manage. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T3#GNS124_U1_T3_h5)

question: Which of these is a classic example of appropriate technology in a Nigerian primary health care setting?

options.A: Oral Rehydration Therapy (ORT) using clean water, salt, and sugar
options.B: A computerized robotic surgical theater in a remote village clinic
options.C: Imported synthetic infant formula distributed without clean water access

explanation: Correct! ORT is a lifesaver because it is scientifically proven, cheap, safe, and mothers can easily mix it at home using everyday ingredients. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T3#GNS124_U1_T3_h5)

question: How does the daily work of a PHC nurse differ mainly from a nurse in a high-tech hospital ICU?

options.A: The hospital nurse spends most of their time farming and digging boreholes
options.B: The PHC nurse focuses heavily on community outreach, health promotion, and preventive education
options.C: The PHC nurse is forbidden from touching patients or administering medications
options.D: The PHC nurse only provides end-of-life care and palliative treatments

explanation: Well done! While hospital nurses focus heavily on treating acute illness, PHC nurses focus on keeping the wider community well through prevention and health education. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T3#GNS124_U1_T3_h6)

question: A nurse in a rural Nigerian clinic notices more waterborne diseases during the rainy season. What action best reflects PHC philosophy?

options.A: Wait inside the clinic and only treat patients who manage to walk in with severe diarrhea
options.B: Collaborate with community leaders to organize safe water education and promote simple water boiling methods
options.C: Complain to the federal government and refuse to see any more sick patients
options.D: Refer every single patient immediately to a foreign overseas hospital

explanation: Spot on! Being proactive with education and community teamwork stops outbreaks at the grassroots before they overwhelm the clinic. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T3#GNS124_U1_T3_h6)

question: What is a major systemic challenge frequently facing primary health care centers in Nigeria today?

options.A: Too many operational hospitals with zero patients
options.B: Excessive supplies of clean water and electricity
options.C: An overwhelming surplus of highly paid medical doctors in every village
options.D: Chronic underfunding and shortages of essential drugs

explanation: Correct. Sadly, many primary health centers struggle with basic funding, poor infrastructure, and running out of essential medicines. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T3#GNS124_U1_T3_h7)

question: Why does the migration of healthcare workers out of rural primary centers severely damage the PHC system?

options.A: It leaves community health facilities understaffed and unable to provide continuous care
options.B: It forces the government to close down all universities in the country
options.C: It increases the cost of building large teaching hospitals in major cities
options.D: It causes patients to stop trusting traditional herbal medicine

explanation: You nailed it! Without skilled nurses on the ground in rural areas, essential services like immunizations, antenatal care, and health education grind to a halt. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T3#GNS124_U1_T3_h7)
